event_param_exploded.name: event_param_exploded
event_param_exploded.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.user_pseudo_id,
  e.event_timestamp,
  e.event_name,
  e.event_bundle_sequence_id,
  ep.key AS param_key,
  ep.value.int_value AS param_int_value,
  ep.value.double_value AS param_double_value,
  ep.value.string_value AS param_string_value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_20210109` AS e,
  UNNEST(e.event_params) AS ep
event_param_exploded.description: One row per event_param key/value for each event row, normalizing the repeated event_params array into rows with numeric and string value columns exposed.

event_engagement_per_event.name: event_engagement_per_event
event_engagement_per_event.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.user_pseudo_id,
  e.event_timestamp,
  e.event_name,
  -- canonicalize engagement_time_msec: prefer int_value, else floor(double_value) cast to INT64, else NULL
  CASE
    WHEN ep.param_int_value IS NOT NULL THEN ep.param_int_value
    WHEN ep.param_double_value IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(FLOOR(ep.param_double_value) AS INT64)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS engagement_time_msec,
  -- carry bundle id to satisfy grain (kept in output so view remains joinable; not requested as output column)
  e.event_bundle_sequence_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_20210109` AS e,
  UNNEST(e.event_params) AS ep_raw
-- normalize event_params into scalar param columns aligned with event_param_exploded shape
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    e2.user_pseudo_id AS user_pseudo_id,
    e2.event_timestamp AS event_timestamp,
    e2.event_name AS event_name,
    ep2.key AS param_key,
    ep2.value.int_value AS param_int_value,
    ep2.value.double_value AS param_double_value,
    ep2.value.string_value AS param_string_value,
    e2.event_bundle_sequence_id AS event_bundle_sequence_id
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_20210109` AS e2,
    UNNEST(e2.event_params) AS ep2
) AS ep
ON e.user_pseudo_id = ep.user_pseudo_id
AND e.event_timestamp = ep.event_timestamp
AND e.event_name = ep.event_name
AND e.event_bundle_sequence_id = ep.event_bundle_sequence_id
AND ep.param_key = 'engagement_time_msec'
WHERE ep.param_key = 'engagement_time_msec'
event_engagement_per_event.description: Per event row, canonicalize engagement_time_msec as a single numeric column (INT64 milliseconds). If both int_value and double_value exist, prefer int_value; if none, NULL. Keeps event-level identifiers and timestamp for time-windowing.

session_products_exploded.name: session_products_exploded
session_products_exploded.body_sql:
SELECT
  fullVisitorId,
  visitId,
  visitStartTime,
  date,
  h.hitNumber AS hitNumber,
  p.v2ProductName AS product_v2ProductName,
  p.productQuantity AS product_productQuantity,
  p.productSKU AS product_productSKU,
  p.productRevenue AS product_productRevenue
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s,
  UNNEST(s.hits) AS h,
  UNNEST(h.product) AS p
session_products_exploded.description: One row per product occurrence within a session hit's product entry. Explodes hits[] -> product[] so each product line on a hit becomes a row with session and hit context and raw product measures.

transaction_revenue_by_traffic_month.name: transaction_revenue_by_traffic_month
transaction_revenue_by_traffic_month.body_sql:
SELECT
  trafficSource.source AS trafficSource_source,
  CAST(SUBSTR(date, 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year,
  CAST(SUBSTR(date, 5, 2) AS INT64) AS month,
  SUM(totals.transactionRevenue) AS monthly_transaction_revenue,
  fullVisitorId,
  visitId,
  visitStartTime,
  date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127`,
  UNNEST([totals]) AS totals,
  UNNEST([trafficSource]) AS trafficSource
WHERE
  totals.transactionRevenue IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  trafficSource.source,
  date,
  fullVisitorId,
  visitId,
  visitStartTime

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic year filter; include all dates so final query can restrict to 2017

transaction_revenue_by_traffic_month.description: Pre-aggregate raw transactionRevenue at the level of traffic source by calendar month. One row per trafficSource.source per month with the summed raw transactionRevenue across all session hits in that month. Keeps raw sums (no scaling) for reuse in yearly or monthly comparisons.

session_level_classified.name: session_level_classified
session_level_classified.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  s.visitId AS visitId,
  s.date AS date,
  SUBSTR(s.date, 1, 6) AS month, -- lift literal: month = first 6 chars of YYYYMMDD date
  COALESCE(s.totals.pageviews, 0) AS pageviews,
  -- is_purchase_session: totals.transactions >= 1 AND there exists at least one product_productRevenue in session > 0
  (SAFE_CAST(s.totals.transactions AS INT64) >= 1
   AND EXISTS (
     SELECT 1
     FROM UNNEST(s.hits) AS h
     WHERE EXISTS (
       SELECT 1
       FROM UNNEST(h.product) AS p
       WHERE COALESCE(p.productRevenue, 0) > 0
     )
  )) AS is_purchase_session,
  -- is_non_purchase_session: totals.transactions IS NULL OR = 0 AND no product.productRevenue present anywhere in session
  ((s.totals.transactions IS NULL OR SAFE_CAST(s.totals.transactions AS INT64) = 0)
   AND NOT EXISTS (
     SELECT 1
     FROM UNNEST(s.hits) AS h2
     WHERE EXISTS (
       SELECT 1
       FROM UNNEST(h2.product) AS p2
       WHERE COALESCE(p2.productRevenue, 0) > 0
     )
  )) AS is_non_purchase_session
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s
WHERE
  s.fullVisitorId IS NOT NULL
session_level_classified.description: One row per session (visit) with canonicalized session identifiers, cleaned pageviews, and boolean flags indicating whether the session qualifies as a purchase session (has totals.transactions >= 1 and at least one product.productRevenue present in any hit) or a non-purchase session (totals.transactions IS NULL OR = 0 and no product.productRevenue present). Excludes sessions with NULL fullVisitorId.

session_hit_product_revenue_flag.name: session_hit_product_revenue_flag
session_hit_product_revenue_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  s.visitId AS visitId,
  h.hitNumber AS hitNumber,
  p.productSKU AS productSKU,
  -- flag true when productRevenue is NOT NULL, false otherwise
  SAFE_CAST(p.productRevenue IS NOT NULL AS BOOL) AS productRevenue_present
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s,
  UNNEST(s.hits) AS h,
  UNNEST(h.product) AS p
session_hit_product_revenue_flag.description: Exploded/normalized rows marking, for each session and each hit-product within that session, whether product.productRevenue is present (non-NULL). This view is a row per session × hit × product indicator useful to determine existence/all-null patterns of productRevenue within a session.

visitor_month_session_class_pageviews.name: visitor_month_session_class_pageviews
visitor_month_session_class_pageviews.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  s.month AS month,
  CASE
    WHEN s.is_purchase_session THEN 'purchase'
    WHEN s.is_non_purchase_session THEN 'non-purchase'
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END AS session_class,
  SUM(s.pageviews) AS visitor_total_pageviews_for_class
FROM
  `session_level_classified` AS s
GROUP BY
  s.fullVisitorId,
  s.month,
  CASE
    WHEN s.is_purchase_session THEN 'purchase'
    WHEN s.is_non_purchase_session THEN 'non-purchase'
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END
visitor_month_session_class_pageviews.description: Per visitor, per month, per session_class (purchase / non-purchase) aggregated visitor-level total pageviews: sums pageviews across that visitor's sessions in that month that belong to the session class. Exposes visitor-month-class totals so downstream queries can compute averages across visitors.

sessions_with_products_in_period.name: sessions_with_products_in_period
sessions_with_products_in_period.body_sql:
SELECT
  sp.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  sp.visitId AS visitId,
  sp.visitStartTime AS visitStartTime,
  sp.date AS date,
  sp.hitNumber AS hits,
  sp.product_v2ProductName AS product_v2ProductName,
  COALESCE(sp.product_productQuantity, 0) AS product_productQuantity
FROM
  `session_products_exploded` AS sp

semantic_filters.date: ANY (caller will filter by date range; do not hardcode)

sessions_with_products_in_period.description: One row per product occurrence within a session (hit-level product record). Exposes visitor, session, product name and quantity for filtering and aggregation by time period.

visitors_who_bought_keyword_product_in_p.name: visitors_who_bought_keyword_product_in_period
visitors_who_bought_keyword_product_in_p.body_sql:
SELECT
  sp.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  -- flag is 1 if the visitor purchased any product whose name contains the keyword (case-insensitive) in the date range
  MAX(IF(
    LOWER(COALESCE(sp.product_v2ProductName, '')) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(@keyword), '%')
    AND PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', sp.date) BETWEEN PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', @start_date) AND PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', @end_date)
    AND COALESCE(sp.product_productQuantity, 0) > 0,
    1, 0
  )) AS bought_keyword_product_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s,
  UNNEST(s.hits) AS h,
  UNNEST(h.product) AS p,
  -- expose product fields in the same names used by downstream helper views for compatibility
  UNNEST([STRUCT(s.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId, s.visitId AS visitId, s.visitStartTime AS visitStartTime, s.date AS date,
               h.hitNumber AS hitNumber,
               p.v2ProductName AS product_v2ProductName,
               p.productQuantity AS product_productQuantity,
               p.productSKU AS product_productSKU,
               p.productRevenue AS product_productRevenue)]) AS sp
GROUP BY
  sp.fullVisitorId

semantic_filters.date: ANY (date range to be provided by caller)
semantic_filters.keyword: ANY (keyword to be provided by caller)

visitors_who_bought_keyword_product_in_p.description: One row per visitor indicating whether they purchased any product whose name contains a specified keyword within a given date range. Intended to quickly filter cohorts of visitors who bought products matching a substring (case-insensitive).

sessions_with_campaign.name: sessions_with_campaign
sessions_with_campaign.body_sql:
SELECT
  fullVisitorId,
  visitId,
  visitStartTime,
  trafficSource.campaign AS trafficSource_campaign
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127`
sessions_with_campaign.description: One row per session (visit) exposing session identifiers and trafficSource campaign for filtering cohorts by campaign.

session_hits_page_events.name: session_hits_page_events
session_hits_page_events.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- session identifiers (carry-through for joinability)
  fullVisitorId,
  visitId,
  visitStartTime,
  -- hit-level ordering from the nested hits array
  h.hitNumber AS hitNumber,
  -- normalized hit type (e.g., PAGE, EVENT, TRANSACTION, ITEM, etc.)
  h.type AS hits_type,
  -- page path exposed from the nested page struct (nullable for non-page hits)
  h.page.pagePath AS page_pagePath,
  -- hit timestamp (milliseconds offset within session as stored in hits.time)
  h.time AS hits_time,
  -- session-level time on site from totals (nullable)
  totals.timeOnSite AS totals_timeOnSite
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s,
  UNNEST(s.hits) AS h
session_hits_page_events.description: Flatten hits array to one row per hit for sessions, exposing hit ordering, hit type, pagePath, and session-level identifiers; normalizes nested fields used for sequencing and time-on-page analysis.

home_page_follow_transitions.name: home_page_follow_transitions
home_page_follow_transitions.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  s.visitId AS visitId,
  s.visitStartTime AS visitStartTime,
  h.hitNumber AS origin_hitNumber,
  h.page.pagePath AS origin_pagePath,
  LEAD(h.hitNumber) OVER (PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId, s.visitId, s.visitStartTime ORDER BY h.hitNumber) AS next_hitNumber,
  LEAD(h.page.pagePath) OVER (PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId, s.visitId, s.visitStartTime ORDER BY h.hitNumber) AS next_pagePath,
  s.totals.timeOnSite AS origin_totals_timeOnSite
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s,
  UNNEST(s.hits) AS h
WHERE
  h.type = "PAGE"
home_page_follow_transitions.description: For sessions with page hits, compute the immediate-next pagePath after each page hit using hitNumber ordering (LEAD). Each row represents a transition from a page hit to its immediate subsequent page hit within the same session.

session_level_clean.name: session_level_clean
session_level_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- keep original key columns for joinability
  visitorId,
  visitId,
  -- date as provided (leave filtering to query-time)
  date,
  -- canonical session-level scalar measures
  SAFE_CAST(totals.pageviews AS INT64) AS pageviews,
  SAFE_CAST(totals.transactions AS INT64) AS transactions
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127`
session_level_clean.description: One row per session with canonicalized key fields and extracted scalar measures needed for session-level analysis (visitor id, session id, date, totals.pageviews, totals.transactions). Filters and question-specific date ranges are left to question_ops.

session_purchase_classification.name: session_purchase_classification
session_purchase_classification.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- keep key columns for joinability
  visitorId,
  visitId,
  date,
  -- numeric pageviews from totals.pageviews (lift literal out of view: none)
  SAFE_CAST(totals.pageviews AS INT64) AS pageviews,
  -- keep raw transactions count
  SAFE_CAST(totals.transactions AS INT64) AS transactions,
  -- classify session: 'purchase' when transactions > 0 else 'non_purchase'
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(totals.transactions AS INT64) > 0 THEN 'purchase'
    ELSE 'non_purchase'
  END AS purchase_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s
session_purchase_classification.description: Session-level cohort that classifies each session as 'purchase' or 'non_purchase' based on totals.transactions, exposing classification and the numeric pageviews measure. Keeps one row per session (visitorId, visitId).

sessions_canonicalized.name: sessions_canonicalized
sessions_canonicalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- identity keys (keep for joinability)
  fullVisitorId,
  visitId,
  visitStartTime,

  -- original date string from source (lifted literal handling done outside the view)
  date,

  -- canonical parsed DATE type from the date string (expected format YYYYMMDD)
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS date_dt,

  -- device mobile flag (carry forward device.isMobile)
  (device.isMobile) AS device_isMobile,

  -- whether the session contains any transaction: any hit with non-null transaction.transactionId
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM UNNEST(hits) AS h
    WHERE h.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
  ) AS has_transaction,

  -- keep raw totals for later aggregations
  totals.pageviews AS totals_pageviews,
  totals.hits AS totals_hits

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127`
sessions_canonicalized.description: One row per session (visit) with normalized/canonicalized core fields: parsed date, visitor id, visit id, device mobile flag, and whether the session contains a transaction (any hit with transaction.transactionId not null). Keeps raw totals for later aggregations.

user_session_transaction_links.name: user_session_transaction_links
user_session_transaction_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  s.visitId AS visitId,
  s.date AS date,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) AS date_dt,
  s.device.isMobile AS device_isMobile,
  TRUE AS transaction_present
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s,
  UNNEST(s.hits) AS h
WHERE
  -- only keep sessions that have at least one transaction recorded on any hit
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM UNNEST(s.hits) AS hh
    WHERE hh.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
    OR (hh.transaction.transactionRevenue IS NOT NULL AND hh.transaction.transactionRevenue != 0)
  )
GROUP BY
  s.fullVisitorId,
  s.visitId,
  s.date,
  s.device.isMobile
user_session_transaction_links.description: One row per session that contains at least one transaction, with the session's date and the fullVisitorId and visitId. Also useful to identify the session(s) where the user's first transaction occurred by ordering per user.

product_action_flagged_by_month.name: product_action_flagged_by_month
product_action_flagged_by_month.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- normalized month in YYYY-MM (lift literals out of view)
  FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date)) AS month,
  fullVisitorId,
  visitId,
  visitStartTime,
  hit.hitNumber AS hit_hitNumber,
  prod.productSKU AS product_productSKU,
  -- impressions are product fields with isImpression = TRUE; we include explicit boolean
  IF(prod.isImpression IS TRUE, TRUE, FALSE) AS is_product_impression,
  -- eCommerceAction.action_type values indicating detail / add / purchase are not hard-coded here.
  -- We infer from the hit's eCommerceAction.action_type:
  --  - detail pageview: action_type = 'detail'
  --  - add to cart: action_type = 'add'
  --  - purchase: action_type = 'purchase' (these literals should be supplied when querying)
  IF(hit.eCommerceAction.action_type = 'detail', TRUE, FALSE) AS is_product_detail_pageview,
  IF(hit.eCommerceAction.action_type = 'add', TRUE, FALSE) AS is_add_to_cart,
  IF(hit.eCommerceAction.action_type = 'purchase', TRUE, FALSE) AS is_purchase,
  -- product quantity (carry through)
  prod.productQuantity AS product_productQuantity
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s,
  UNNEST(s.hits) AS hit,
  UNNEST(hit.product) AS prod
WHERE
  -- exclude product impressions from the primary normalized product rows when desired;
  -- keep all rows but this view normalizes flags — no literal exclusion here so callers can filter by is_product_impression = FALSE
  TRUE

semantic_filters.exclude_product_impressions: hits.product.isImpression IS NULL OR hits.product.isImpression = FALSE

product_action_flagged_by_month.description: Project and normalize each product-occurrence row into a canonical set of columns including normalized month (YYYY-MM) and boolean flags for product-detail pageview, add-to-cart, and purchase based on eCommerceAction.action_type; excludes product impressions.

visitors_sessions_basic.name: visitors_sessions_basic
visitors_sessions_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  fullVisitorId,
  visitId,
  visitNumber,
  visitStartTime,
  date,
  device.deviceCategory AS device_deviceCategory,
  totals.transactions AS totals_transactions,
  totals.transactionRevenue AS totals_transactionRevenue,
  totals.pageviews AS totals_pageviews
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127`
visitors_sessions_basic.description: One row per session/visit with canonicalized identifiers and key session-level attributes (date, device category, visitId, visitStartTime, fullVisitorId, visitNumber, totals.pageviews, totals.transactions, totals.transactionRevenue). Useful as a cleaned session-level base for visitor/session cohorts and joins with nested hits/products.

visitor_first_visit.name: visitor_first_visit
visitor_first_visit.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  FIRST_VALUE(s.visitId) OVER (PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId ORDER BY s.visitStartTime ASC, s.visitId ASC) AS first_visitId,
  FIRST_VALUE(s.visitStartTime) OVER (PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId ORDER BY s.visitStartTime ASC, s.visitId ASC) AS first_visitStartTime,
  FIRST_VALUE(s.date) OVER (PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId ORDER BY s.visitStartTime ASC, s.visitId ASC) AS first_date,
  FIRST_VALUE(s.device.deviceCategory) OVER (PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId ORDER BY s.visitStartTime ASC, s.visitId ASC) AS first_device_deviceCategory,
  FIRST_VALUE(s.visitNumber) OVER (PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId ORDER BY s.visitStartTime ASC, s.visitId ASC) AS first_visitNumber
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s
GROUP BY
  s.fullVisitorId,
  s.visitId,
  s.visitStartTime,
  s.date,
  s.device.deviceCategory,
  s.visitNumber
visitor_first_visit.description: First recorded visit per visitor (earliest visitStartTime). Exposes the visitor id and their first visit's identifying columns (visitId, visitStartTime, date, device category) so downstream queries can compare later sessions to the first visit.

visitor_transaction_sessions.name: visitor_transaction_sessions
visitor_transaction_sessions.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS fullVisitorId,
  visitId,
  visitStartTime,
  date,
  device.deviceCategory AS device_deviceCategory,
  totals.transactions AS totals_transactions,
  totals.transactionRevenue AS totals_transactionRevenue
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127`
WHERE
  -- Session-level transactions > 0 (lift literal out of view if needed)
  SAFE_CAST(totals.transactions AS INT64) > 0
visitor_transaction_sessions.description: Sessions that contain at least one transaction (session-level transactions > 0). One row per transactional session with the visitor id, visitId, visitStartTime, date and device category and raw transaction revenue. Useful to identify first transaction session per visitor and attributes of that session.

ga_visitor_first_session.name: ga_visitor_first_session
ga_visitor_first_session.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  s.visitId AS first_visitId,
  s.visitStartTime AS first_visitStartTime,
  s.date AS first_date,
  s.totals.timeOnSite AS first_timeOnSite,
  s.totals.transactions AS first_totals_transactions
FROM (
  -- pick each visitor's earliest session (by visitStartTime). break ties by smallest visitId.
  SELECT
    fullVisitorId,
    ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT(visitId, visitStartTime, date, totals) ORDER BY visitStartTime ASC, visitId ASC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)].visitId AS visitId,
    ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT(visitId, visitStartTime, date, totals) ORDER BY visitStartTime ASC, visitId ASC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)].visitStartTime AS visitStartTime,
    ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT(visitId, visitStartTime, date, totals) ORDER BY visitStartTime ASC, visitId ASC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)].date AS date,
    ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT(visitId, visitStartTime, date, totals) ORDER BY visitStartTime ASC, visitId ASC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)].totals AS totals
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127`
  GROUP BY fullVisitorId
) s
ga_visitor_first_session.description: Per-visitor first session (earliest visitStartTime) with key session attributes: first_visit_start_time, first_visit_date, first_timeOnSite, first_totals_transactions. One row per visitor for use in cohort selection (e.g., new users whose first session date falls in a given window).

ga_visitor_later_purchase_flag.name: ga_visitor_later_purchase_flag
ga_visitor_later_purchase_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  -- Whether the visitor has ANY purchase session that occurs after a reference visitStartTime.
  -- Note: comparison to a reference visitStartTime is done outside this view; this field is TRUE if there exists any session with purchase visitStartTime > reference.
  -- We expose it as a boolean indicating existence of any purchase at a later time than some external reference.
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS gs2,
         UNNEST(gs2.hits) AS h2
    WHERE gs2.fullVisitorId = s.fullVisitorId
      -- evidence of purchase: either transaction present at session-level totals.transactionRevenue > 0
      -- or any hit contains a transaction.transactionId or item with itemQuantity/productRevenue.
      AND (
        IFNULL(gs2.totals.transactionRevenue, 0) > 0
        OR h2.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
        OR EXISTS(
          SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(h2.product) AS p2
          WHERE IFNULL(p2.productQuantity, 0) > 0 OR IFNULL(p2.productRevenue, 0) != 0
        )
      )
  ) AS has_any_later_purchase,
  -- The earliest (minimum) visitStartTime among sessions that show purchase evidence for this visitor.
  -- Consumers can compare this timestamp to their reference session's visitStartTime.
  (
    SELECT
      MIN(visitStartTime)
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS gs3,
         UNNEST(gs3.hits) AS h3
    WHERE gs3.fullVisitorId = s.fullVisitorId
      AND (
        IFNULL(gs3.totals.transactionRevenue, 0) > 0
        OR h3.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
        OR EXISTS(
          SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(h3.product) AS p3
          WHERE IFNULL(p3.productQuantity, 0) > 0 OR IFNULL(p3.productRevenue, 0) != 0
        )
      )
  ) AS first_purchase_visitStartTime_after_reference
FROM (
  -- Base set of distinct visitors (one row per visitor)
  SELECT DISTINCT fullVisitorId
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127`
) AS s
ga_visitor_later_purchase_flag.description: For each visitor (fullVisitorId), indicates whether they have any session after a provided first_visitStartTime that contains evidence of a purchase. Does NOT bake in the first_visitStartTime value; instead exposes per-session visitStartTime and purchase indicators to be compared/joined to a first-session table. Useful to test if a purchase occurred after a particular session.

inpatient_charge_rows_2014_cohort.name: inpatient_charge_rows_2014_cohort

drg_total_discharges_by_drg.name: drg_total_discharges_by_drg

drg_city_discharge_and_weighted_payments.description: For each DRG definition and provider_city, compute sum of total_discharges and the weighted sum needed to compute weighted average of average_total_payments (weights = total_discharges). One row per drg_definition + provider_city. Useful to rank cities by discharges for a DRG and to compute city-level weighted averages.

provider_outpatient_payments_by_provider.name: provider_outpatient_payments_by_provider

provider_outpatient_payments_by_provider.description: Per provider, the mean of outpatient average_total_payments across all outpatient records (one row per provider from outpatient_charges_2012). Keeps provider identifiers and name for joins.

provider_inpatient_payments_by_provider.name: provider_inpatient_payments_by_provider
provider_inpatient_payments_by_provider.body_sql:
SELECT

provider_combined_payments.name: provider_combined_payments
provider_combined_payments.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- keep provider_id as the key (string in source outpatient/inpatient tables)
  COALESCE(o.provider_id, i.provider_id) AS provider_id,
  -- prefer outpatient provider_name; fall back to inpatient
  COALESCE(o.provider_name, i.provider_name) AS provider_name,
  -- outpatient average total payments per provider (from outpatient table)
  o.average_total_payments AS outpatient_average_total_payments,
  -- inpatient average total payments per provider (from inpatient table)
  i.average_total_payments AS inpatient_average_total_payments,
  -- combined: average of the two averages when both present; otherwise whichever exists
  CASE
    WHEN o.average_total_payments IS NOT NULL AND i.average_total_payments IS NOT NULL
      THEN (o.average_total_payments + i.average_total_payments) / 2
    WHEN o.average_total_payments IS NOT NULL THEN o.average_total_payments
    ELSE i.average_total_payments
  END AS combined_average_total_payments
FROM
  -- outpatient charges 2012 (source table name must match DDL exactly)
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_2012` AS o
FULL JOIN
  -- inpatient charges 2013 (source table name must match DDL exactly)
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_2013` AS i
ON o.provider_id = i.provider_id
provider_combined_payments.description: Denormalized per-provider row combining outpatient and inpatient per-provider average_total_payments (one row per provider). Intended to be used to compute combined measures and ranking across providers.

drug_exposure_with_person_location_and_d.name: drug_exposure_with_person_location_and_dates
drug_exposure_with_person_location_and_d.body_sql:

  COALESCE(CAST(de.drug_exposure_start_datetime AS DATE), de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS drug_exposure_start_date,
  COALESCE(CAST(de.drug_exposure_end_datetime AS DATE), de.drug_exposure_end_date, de.verbatim_end_date) AS drug_exposure_end_date,
  p.location_id,
  p.state
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` AS de
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` AS per
ON
  de.person_id = per.person_id
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.location` AS p
ON
  per.location_id = p.location_id

semantic_filters.person.location_id IS NOT NULL: retain exposures only when a linked person has a location_id (location lookup may still yield NULL state)
semantic_filters.drug_exposure_start_date IS NOT NULL: only exposures with a start date

drug_exposure_with_person_location_and_d.description: One row per drug_exposure enriched with the person's location (state) and canonical start/end dates and identifiers needed for linking costs and concepts. Keeps raw exposure-level data for flexible aggregation by drug, person, or state.

semantic_filters.total_cost IS NOT NULL: cost rows may have NULLs; include them but raw value retained (caller may treat missing as zero)

drug_exposure_cost_linked.description: Cost rows linked to drug exposures via cost_event_id = drug_exposure.drug_exposure_id. Keeps raw cost amounts and domain id so callers can restrict to drug-related cost_domain_id values. Each row represents one cost record connected to one drug_exposure.

concept_minimal.name: concept_minimal

inpatient_record_costs.name: inpatient_record_costs
inpatient_record_costs.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  provider_name,
  drg_definition,
  hospital_referral_region_description,
  total_discharges,
  average_medicare_payments,
  -- canonical per-record inpatient Medicare cost (lift literal multiplication out of downstream queries)
  (average_medicare_payments * total_discharges) AS inpatient_record_medicare_cost,
  -- source year for this table instance
  2013 AS source_year
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_2013`
WHERE
  -- exclude rows where either multiplicand is NULL so cost is well-defined
  average_medicare_payments IS NOT NULL
  AND total_discharges IS NOT NULL
inpatient_record_costs.description: Per-row inpatient record with canonical per-record inpatient Medicare cost computed (average_medicare_payments * total_discharges). Keeps original provider and DRG details and preserves rows for later aggregation. Excludes rows where either multiplicand is NULL so cost is well-defined.

outpatient_record_costs.name: outpatient_record_costs
outpatient_record_costs.body_sql:
SELECT
  oc.provider_id,
  oc.provider_name,
  oc.apc,
  oc.hospital_referral_region,
  oc.outpatient_services,
  oc.average_total_payments,
  -- canonical per-record outpatient cost (lifted literal: multiply payments * count)
  oc.average_total_payments * oc.outpatient_services AS outpatient_record_cost,
  -- source year lifted out as a column value; keep it literal-free inside view definition consumers can filter
  2012 AS source_year
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_2012` AS oc
WHERE
  -- exclude rows where either multiplicand is NULL
  oc.outpatient_services IS NOT NULL
  AND oc.average_total_payments IS NOT NULL
outpatient_record_costs.description: Per-row outpatient record with canonical per-record outpatient cost computed (average_total_payments * outpatient_services). Keeps provider metadata and APC info. Excludes rows where either multiplicand is NULL.

provider_yearly_inpatient_aggregates.name: provider_yearly_inpatient_aggregates
provider_yearly_inpatient_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATE) AS source_year,
  SUM(average_medicare_payments) AS yearly_sum_inpatient_medicare_cost,
  AVG(average_medicare_payments) AS yearly_avg_inpatient_record_cost,
  provider_name
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_2013`
-- NOTE: lift year literal out of the view; this table is 2013 so DATE is synthesized from that year.
CROSS JOIN UNNEST([DATE '2013-01-01']) AS DATE
GROUP BY provider_id, source_year, provider_name
provider_yearly_inpatient_aggregates.description: Aggregated inpatient measures per provider per calendar year: SUM of inpatient_record_medicare_cost (for computing multi-year totals) and AVG of inpatient_record_medicare_cost (yearly average). Groups at provider_id + year so it can be joined to outpatient yearly aggregates and ranked across years or across the 2011-2015 span.

standard_condition_occurrences_by_person.name: standard_condition_occurrences_by_person
standard_condition_occurrences_by_person.body_sql:

WHERE

standard_condition_occurrences_by_person.description: Condition occurrence rows where the condition_concept_id is a standard concept (standard_concept='S'). Exposes one row per condition_occurrence and includes person linkage and concept id for joins to disease concept sets. Useful as the base cohort of condition events for counting persons with specific condition concept memberships.

person_core.name: person_core
person_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.person_id AS person_id,
  p.year_of_birth AS year_of_birth,
  p.month_of_birth AS month_of_birth,
  p.day_of_birth AS day_of_birth,
  p.birth_datetime AS birth_datetime,
  p.gender_concept_id AS gender_concept_id,
  p.gender_source_value AS gender_source_value,
  p.race_concept_id AS race_concept_id,
  p.ethnicity_concept_id AS ethnicity_concept_id,
  p.location_id AS location_id,
  p.provider_id AS provider_id,
  p.care_site_id AS care_site_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` AS p
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation_period` AS op
ON
  p.person_id = op.person_id
-- The LEFT JOIN to observation_period preserves person rows even if no period exists,
-- and keeps the view joinable for analyses needing observation windows.
GROUP BY
  p.person_id,
  p.year_of_birth,
  p.month_of_birth,
  p.day_of_birth,
  p.birth_datetime,
  p.gender_concept_id,
  p.gender_source_value,
  p.race_concept_id,
  p.ethnicity_concept_id,
  p.location_id,
  p.provider_id,
  p.care_site_id
person_core.description: Canonical person-level row with primary identifiers and birth/gender/race source fields for downstream cohorting and joins.

drug_exposure_by_person.name: drug_exposure_by_person

drug_era_by_person.name: drug_era_by_person

hurricane_point_rows.name: hurricane_point_rows
hurricane_point_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid,
  season,
  basin,
  name,
  iso_time,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  etl_timestamp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
WHERE
  latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
hurricane_point_rows.description: Row-level cohort of raw hurricane track observations (one row per recorded observation point). Filters out rows missing latitude or longitude to support geodesic computations and exposes identity, time, location, and nominal attributes for downstream ranking/aggregation.

storms_total_travel_distance_per_storm.name: storms_total_travel_distance_per_storm
storms_total_travel_distance_per_storm.body_sql:
SELECT
  h.sid,
  h.name,
  h.season,
  h.number,
  ROUND(SUM(ST_DISTANCE(
    ST_GEOGPOINT(prev.longitude, prev.latitude),
    ST_GEOGPOINT(curr.longitude, curr.latitude)
  ))/1000, 3) AS total_travel_km
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes` AS h
-- derive ordered track points per storm, keeping only non-null lat/lon and using iso_time ordering
JOIN (
  SELECT
    sid,
    iso_time,
    latitude,
    longitude,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS rn
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
  WHERE
    latitude IS NOT NULL
    AND longitude IS NOT NULL
) AS curr
  ON curr.sid = h.sid
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    sid,
    iso_time,
    latitude,
    longitude,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS rn
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
  WHERE
    latitude IS NOT NULL
    AND longitude IS NOT NULL
) AS prev
  ON prev.sid = curr.sid
  AND prev.rn = curr.rn - 1
WHERE
  curr.latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND curr.longitude IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  h.sid, h.name, h.season, h.number
storms_total_travel_distance_per_storm.description: Total travel distance per storm computed as the sum of geodesic distances between consecutive track points (points with non-null lat/lon) ordered by iso_time. Produces one row per storm (sid) with raw measure total_travel_km for ranking storms by distance.

storms_event_rows.name: storms_event_rows
storms_event_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  episode_id,
  event_id,
  -- canonicalized state: use as-is from source; kept for joinability
  state,
  -- keep original event_begin_time (DATETIME)
  event_begin_time,
  -- extract year from event_begin_time for easy grouping/filtering
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM event_begin_time) AS event_year
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.storms_1963`
WHERE
  -- exclude rows missing state or event_begin_time to satisfy cohort definition
  state IS NOT NULL
  AND event_begin_time IS NOT NULL
  -- ensure one row per event_id: if duplicate event_id rows exist in the table,
  -- prefer the first non-null event_begin_time. Use ROW_NUMBER() over partition
  -- to deduplicate deterministically by event_begin_time ascending and episode_id.
QUALIFY
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY event_id
    ORDER BY event_begin_time ASC, episode_id ASC
  ) = 1
storms_event_rows.description: Row-level cohort of storm events with canonicalized state and event date components; filters out rows missing state or event_begin_time. Keeps one row per event occurrence.

storms_event_counts_per_state_year.name: storms_event_counts_per_state_year
storms_event_counts_per_state_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  state,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM event_begin_time) AS event_year,
  COUNT(1) AS events_in_year
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.storms_1963`
WHERE
  state IS NOT NULL
  AND event_begin_time IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  state,
  event_year
storms_event_counts_per_state_year.description: Per-calendar-year counts of storm events per state. Aggregates the row-level storm events into (state, event_year) counts.

stations_operational_period.name: stations_operational_period
stations_operational_period.body_sql:
SELECT
  usaf,
  wban,
  -- parse 'begin' which is formatted like YYYYMMDD or possibly empty/null -> convert to DATE or NULL
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', NULLIF(begin, '')) AS parsed_begin_date,
  -- parse 'end' similarly; treat empty or NULL as NULL (ongoing)
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', NULLIF(`end`, '')) AS parsed_end_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`
stations_operational_period.description: Station operational period expressed with canonical start and end dates (as DATE or NULL). One row per station with computed parsed_begin and parsed_end to enable date-range filters (treat empty or NULL end as ongoing/null).

stations_location_identifiers.name: stations_location_identifiers
stations_location_identifiers.body_sql:
SELECT

  wban,

  lat,

  country,
  state,
  call
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`
stations_location_identifiers.description: Station identity and location columns useful for joins to daily observations: exposes station keys and spatial columns without changing them.

gsod_daily_observations.name: gsod_daily_observations
gsod_daily_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  stn,
  year,
  mo,
  da,
  temp,
  wdsp,
  prcp,
  count_temp,
  -- count_wdsp is stored as STRING in the source; carry it through as-is to preserve raw sentinel values
  count_wdsp,
  flag_prcp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2000`
gsod_daily_observations.description: One row per station-day observation from the GSOD daily table, exposing raw measured columns and raw sentinel values (no imputation). Useful as the base cohort for filtering by station, date parts, and applying cleaning/aggregation later.

gsod_daily_observations_cleaned.name: gsod_daily_observations_cleaned
gsod_daily_observations_cleaned.body_sql:
SELECT
  stn,
  year,
  mo,
  da,
  -- temp: sentinel 9999.9 -> NULL, otherwise keep as FLOAT64
  CASE
    WHEN temp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN temp = 9999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE temp
  END AS temp_clean,
  -- wdsp is stored as STRING; cast to FLOAT64, treat missing/invalid/999.9 as NULL
  CASE
    WHEN wdsp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(wdsp) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) = 999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64)
  END AS wdsp_clean,
  -- prcp: sentinel 99.99 -> NULL, otherwise keep as FLOAT64
  CASE
    WHEN prcp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN prcp = 99.99 THEN NULL
    ELSE prcp
  END AS prcp_clean,
  flag_prcp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2000`
gsod_daily_observations_cleaned.description: Normalized/cleaned per station-day observations: casts sentinel missing values to NULL and casts wind speed column to numeric. Keeps one row per station-day. Designed so downstream aggregations can rely on NULLs for missing data.
